title: Security Testing & Incident Response
description: Study adversarial test corpora, security telemetry and alerting, incident containment and recovery, and regression gates and residual risk. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Adversarial test corpora
lessons.description: Define the expected blocked action and observable pass condition.
lessons.conceptOverview: Build authorized test fixtures around trust crossings and expected denied actions. Record success criteria and sanitize examples so tests are repeatable without accessing real sensitive data.
lessons.whyItMatters: Security fixtures should test behavior with controlled data.

lessons.title: Security telemetry and alerting
lessons.description: Choose correlation fields and an alert threshold with a review path.
lessons.conceptOverview: Log relevant action metadata, denials and unusual access patterns without retaining unnecessary secrets. Correlate attempts across a run so repeated boundary probing can be investigated.
lessons.whyItMatters: Useful security telemetry connects actions while minimizing sensitive payloads.

lessons.title: Incident containment and recovery
lessons.description: Write immediate containment steps and a verification gate for restoration.
lessons.conceptOverview: Contain an incident by restricting affected capabilities, preserving relevant evidence and identifying exposed data. Recovery includes fixing the path, rotating affected credentials and verifying the control before re-enabling access.
lessons.whyItMatters: Restoration should follow containment and validated remediation.

lessons.title: Regression gates and residual risk
lessons.description: Add variant fixtures and record the remaining uncertainty.
lessons.conceptOverview: Security tests show behavior on tested cases rather than universal immunity. Keep regression suites for discovered failures and document remaining exposure with accountable owners.
lessons.whyItMatters: Passing known tests does not prove all attacks are impossible.
